title: David Garibaldi (musician) - Wikipedia
notes: John David Garibaldi, born 4 November 1946, Oakland, California. Piano and violin before percussion at ten; a kit at fifteen, taught by ear from records; his high school big band; Eddie Tinga gave him his kit. Chabot College; saw James Brown's band rehearse in San Jose; The Disciples to 1966. The Air Force (Lackland; McChord, Tacoma: timpani, snare and mallets in a symphonic band), discharged December 1969. Joined Tower of Power in July 1970; left in the mid-1970s; back in 1998; retired from the band 15 January 2024. Also Gino Vannelli, Patti Austin, Natalie Cole, Boz Scaggs, the Yellowjackets, Jermaine Jackson, Deniece Williams; Talking Drums; the books Future Sounds and The Funky Beat; a Modern Drummer column. Influences: Sonny Payne, Greg Errico, Bernard Purdie, Zigaboo Modeliste, Clyde Stubblefield; also Melvin Parker, Jamal Thomas, Orestes Vilato, Tony Williams, Elvin Jones. 'All I did was take what I liked from about six or seven of my favorite drummers.' He 'avoided the standard accentuation of the second and fourth beat with the snare drum' for 'a more repetitive pattern that resets itself after a few bars' (citing Meronuck, 2015). Mark Griffith (PAS): 'a funky sixteenth-note based groove that has all or most of the notes played separately with backbeats.' Purdie: 'I'm absolutely certain David influenced drummers all over.' Castillo: 'He always has to be unique and that doesn't fit in with other people who all they want is just a timekeeper.' Rolling Stone's 100 greatest drummers, number 46.

title: Tower of Power - Wikipedia
notes: The Oakland horn band led by Emilio Castillo and Stephen "Doc" Kupka; Garibaldi in the 1970 line-up and back from 1998; hit by an Amtrak train on 12 January 2017 and back in the line-up later that year. Studio albums East Bay Grease (1970), Bump City (1972), Tower of Power (1973), Back to Oakland (1974), Urban Renewal and In the Slot (1975) and on; Pete Antunes on drums from 2024.

title: Bump City - Wikipedia
notes: Released May 1972, Warner Bros. Recorded 1971 to 1972 at Trans Maximus, Memphis; produced by Ron Capone and the band, mixed by Capone and Steve Cropper. Tracks include You Got to Funkifize, Down to the Nightclub, You're Still a Young Man. Rick Stevens lead vocals; Francis Rocco Prestia bass; David Garibaldi drums; Brent Byars congas.

title: Tower of Power (album) - Wikipedia
notes: Released May 1973, Warner Bros.; recorded at Wally Heider Studios, San Francisco; supervising producer Emilio Castillo, recorded by Jim Gaines. What Is Hip? (Castillo, Kupka, Garibaldi), Clever Girl, This Time It's Real, So Very Hard to Go (number 17, July 1973), Soul Vaccination, Clean Slate and others. Lenny Williams lead vocals; Chester Thompson organ; Bruce Conte guitar; Rocco Prestia bass; David Garibaldi drums; Brent Byars congas. Gold.

title: Back to Oakland - Wikipedia
notes: Released February 1974, Warner Bros.; recorded at the Record Plant, Sausalito, and Kaye/Smith, Seattle. Opens with Oakland Stroke... (0:53) and closes with ...Oakland Stroke (1:08); Don't Change Horses, Can't You See (You Doin' Me Wrong), Squib Cakes. David Garibaldi drums.

title: Urban Renewal (Tower of Power album) - Wikipedia
notes: Released January 1975. David Bartlett is the drummer on every track but Willing to Learn, the first single, which is Garibaldi's: so Only So Much Oil in the Ground is not his.

title: David Garibaldi's 12 funk drumming tips
notes: MusicRadar; only the opening was readable. 'The root R&B concept is no fills. Zero. None.' 'When I started playing more fills and being more concerned about that than the groove, I think my playing suffered.'

title: Tower of Power's 'The Skunk, the Goose and the Fly' from East Bay Grease, drummer David Garibaldi
notes: Modern Drummer, 1 June 2026, transcribed by Marc Atkinson; paywalled past the opening, which says he joined on 23 July 1970 after the producer demanded a drummer change before the first album.

title: David Garibaldi: Off the Record (Alfred Music, 2016)
notes: Ten Tower of Power drum transcriptions 'personally transcribed by David Garibaldi', each with an analysis of his approach: Knock Yourself Out, Down to the Nightclub, Soul Vaccination, What Is Hip?, Can't You See (You Doin' Me Wrong), Don't Change Horses, Squib Cakes, On the Serious Side, Vuela Por Noche, Drop It in the Slot. Not read: only its contents are online.

title: David Garibaldi: Tower of Groove (Alfred, excerpt)
notes: Alfred Music Lessons, 2012 upload of the DVD (2007): he plays the Soul Vaccination groove ("Ex. 9") slowly on camera; the DVD breaks down seven Tower of Power grooves.

title: Big Fat Five: David Garibaldi of Tower of Power shares his top five influential records
notes: The Drum Click, 7 May 2025: Count Basie's Breakfast Dance and Barbecue (Sonny Payne), Sly and the Family Stone's A Whole New Thing (Greg Errico), Aretha Franklin Live at Fillmore West (Bernard Purdie), the Meters' Look-Ka Py Py (Zigaboo Modeliste), James Brown's I Got the Feelin' (Clyde Stubblefield). His comments are in the audio, not the page.

title: What Is Hip? David Garibaldi: His Musical Life, His Influences, and His Contributions (Jeremy Meronuck, DMA dissertation, UNLV, 2015)
notes: Interviews with him and his bandmates; the source Wikipedia cites for his style and the Purdie and Castillo quotes. The PDF was refused to us (403): read through Wikipedia only.

title: Tower of Power live at Soul Train, November 1973
notes: Episode 79, aired 17 November 1973: This Time It's Real, So Very Hard to Go, What Is Hip?; the band introduced one by one. Him at the kit at 0:50 and 2:55: dark curls below the ears, a thick moustache, a check shirt; white pearl shells, brass cymbals.

title: Tower of Power on Don Kirshner's Rock Concert, 1973
notes: Get Yo' Feet Back on the Ground and Soul Vaccination, uploaded 2023 and dated 1973 by its title; him only from behind, at 5:20 to 5:35, in a red check shirt.
